index 83f21f3..653e39e 100755
--- a/plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh
+++ b/plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh
@@ -1599,7 +1599,108 @@ elif ! e2e_cmd="$(bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-e2e-entrypoint.sh" "${_lv2_e2e_root
   _dl_note refused no_e2e_entrypoint "repo=${repo}"
   exit 4
 else
-  { printf 'e2e-root: %s\n' "${_lv2_e2e_root}"; ( cd "${_lv2_e2e_root}" && bash -c "${e2e_cmd} --scope changed" ); } > "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log" 2>&1; e2e_rc=$?
+  # E2E-GATE-ARCH-01: serialize the e2e gate with a GLOBAL flock so only one
+  # gate runs at a time across all lanes. Without this, concurrent gate
+  # invocations share temp dirs and working-tree state → flaky e2e_regression
+  # deaths (SD-E2E-GATE-LOAD-FLAKE-01: dispatch-051b9490, -54aaa0bf 2026-08-12).
+  # Lock under ~/.claude/cache/, bounded timeout.  A gate must never run
+  # unlocked: contention is an infrastructure condition, not a regression.
+  _lv2_e2e_lock="${LEADV2_E2E_GATE_LOCK:-${HOME}/.claude/cache/leadv2-e2e-gate.lock}"
+  _lv2_e2e_lock_timeout="${LEADV2_E2E_GATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT:-300}"
+  [[ "${_lv2_e2e_lock_timeout}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || _lv2_e2e_lock_timeout=300
+  _lv2_e2e_lock_dir="${_lv2_e2e_lock}.d"
+  _lv2_e2e_lock_kind=""
+
+  # Returns: 0 acquired; 1 held; 2 lock infrastructure fault.  mkdir is the
+  # portable fallback for stock macOS, which does not ship flock.  Its pid
+  # marker lets a later caller recover a lock left by a crashed owner.
+  _lv2_e2e_mkdir_lock() { # <wait-seconds>
+    local _wait="$1" _started="${SECONDS}" _pid=""
+    while :; do
+      if mkdir "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}" 2>/dev/null; then
+        if ! printf '%s\n' "${BASHPID}" > "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}/pid" 2>/dev/null; then
+          rmdir "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}" 2>/dev/null || true
+          return 2
+        fi
+        _lv2_e2e_lock_kind="mkdir"
+        return 0
+      fi
+      [[ -d "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}" ]] || return 2
+      if [[ -f "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}/pid" ]]; then
+        IFS= read -r _pid < "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}/pid" || _pid=""
+        if [[ "${_pid}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ! kill -0 "${_pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
+          echo "e2e_gate: removing stale portable lock pid=${_pid}"
+          rm -f -- "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}/pid" 2>/dev/null || return 2
+          rmdir "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}" 2>/dev/null || true
+          continue
+        fi
+      fi
+      (( SECONDS - _started >= _wait )) && return 1
+      sleep 1
+    done
+  }
+  _lv2_e2e_release_lock() {
+    if [[ "${_lv2_e2e_lock_kind}" == "mkdir" ]]; then
+      rm -f -- "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}/pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+      rmdir "${_lv2_e2e_lock_dir}" 2>/dev/null || true
+    fi
+  }
+  _lv2_e2e_acquire_lock() { # <wait-seconds>
+    local _wait="$1"
+    _lv2_e2e_lock_kind=""
+    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      exec 9>"${_lv2_e2e_lock}" || return 2
+      flock -x -w "${_wait}" 9 && { _lv2_e2e_lock_kind="flock"; return 0; }
+      return 1
+    fi
+    _lv2_e2e_mkdir_lock "${_wait}"
+  }
+  _lv2_e2e_run() {
+    printf 'e2e-root: %s\n' "${_lv2_e2e_root}"
+    ( cd "${_lv2_e2e_root}" && bash -c "${e2e_cmd} --scope changed" )
+  }
+  _lv2_e2e_infra() { # <detail>
+    local _detail="$1"
+    rm -f "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate-passed.flag"
+    printf 'status: blocked\nreason: e2e_infra\ndetail: %s\n' "${_detail}" > "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.md" 2>/dev/null || true
+    emit decision "e2e_gate task=${TASK} status=blocked reason=e2e_infra detail=${_detail}"
+    _dl_note parked e2e_infra "detail=${_detail}"
+    exit 4
+  }
+
+  # Do not let a failed log or lock-file redirect turn into a suite failure.
+  # The journal line remains available even if the handoff filesystem is bad.
+  if ! mkdir -p "$(dirname "${_lv2_e2e_lock}")" 2>/dev/null; then
+    _lv2_e2e_infra lock_parent_create_failed
+  elif ! : > "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log" 2>/dev/null; then
+    _lv2_e2e_infra e2e_log_create_failed
+  fi
+  if ! command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "e2e_gate: flock unavailable; using portable mkdir lock fallback" >> "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log"
+    emit decision "e2e_gate task=${TASK} status=running lock=mkdir_fallback reason=no_flock"
+  fi
+  if _lv2_e2e_acquire_lock "${_lv2_e2e_lock_timeout}" >> "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log" 2>&1; then
+    _lv2_e2e_run >> "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log" 2>&1; e2e_rc=$?
+    _lv2_e2e_release_lock
+  else
+    _lv2_e2e_lock_rc=$?
+    if [[ ${_lv2_e2e_lock_rc} -eq 2 ]]; then
+      _lv2_e2e_infra lock_acquire_failed
+    fi
+    # A bounded wait has elapsed.  Park/requeue once, then make only an
+    # immediate second acquisition after jitter: do not double a 300s wait.
+    echo "e2e_gate: e2e_gate_lock_timeout attempt=1; parking and retrying after jitter" >> "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log"
+    emit decision "e2e_gate task=${TASK} status=parked reason=e2e_gate_lock_timeout attempt=1 retry=after_jitter"
+    sleep "${LEADV2_E2E_GATE_LOCK_JITTER:-1}"
+    if _lv2_e2e_acquire_lock 0 >> "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log" 2>&1; then
+      _lv2_e2e_run >> "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log" 2>&1; e2e_rc=$?
+      _lv2_e2e_release_lock
+    else
+      _lv2_e2e_lock_rc=$?
+      [[ ${_lv2_e2e_lock_rc} -eq 2 ]] && _lv2_e2e_infra lock_acquire_failed
+      _lv2_e2e_infra e2e_gate_lock_timeout
+    fi
+  fi
   # GATE-FOREIGN-FAILURE-01: WRITES_CSV present + ownership enabled means the
   # passed sentinel is stamped as scoped to the lane's own write set (the
   # apparatus that can tell "my regression" from "someone else's unfinished

# Verify: flock fd 9 never released

Finding: `_lv2_e2e_release_lock` only releases the mkdir-fallback lock; the flock path leaks fd 9.

- `_lv2_e2e_acquire_lock` (diff +56..+65) runs `exec 9>"${_lv2_e2e_lock}"` in the *current* shell
  (plain function, no subshell), then `flock -x -w "${_wait}" 9`, sets `_lv2_e2e_lock_kind="flock"`.
- `_lv2_e2e_release_lock` (diff +50..+55) body is guarded entirely by
  `if [[ "${_lv2_e2e_lock_kind}" == "mkdir" ]]`. There is no `exec 9>&-`, no `flock -u 9`,
  and no `else` arm. For `kind=flock` the function is a no-op.
- No `exec 9>&-` exists anywhere else in the new hunk. The only `9>&-` in the file is the
  pre-existing ledger call at `leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh:81`, which is unrelated
  (and predates the hunk).
- Because the exclusive lock lives on the open file description of fd 9, and fd 9 stays open
  for the life of the top-level `product-close.sh` process, the global gate lock is held past
  the e2e run: e2e-ownership stamping, then the review engine invocation
  (`leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh:1703`, `bash "${_ENGINE_BIN}" ...`) and everything up to
  `exit ${_engine_rc}` at the end of the review branch.
- Consequence matches the claim: a second concurrent lane's `flock -x -w 300` waits on a lock
  held through the whole review, hits the timeout path, and is classified by
  `_lv2_e2e_infra e2e_gate_lock_timeout` — a false `e2e_infra` park, not real gate contention.

## Refutation attempts, all failed

1. *"`exec 9>` inside a function only affects a subshell"* — false; `_lv2_e2e_acquire_lock` is
   invoked as a plain command in the main shell (`if _lv2_e2e_acquire_lock ... ; then`), so the
   redirect mutates the script's own fd table. The `>> log 2>&1` on the call site redirects only
   fd 1/2.
2. *"the process exits right after the e2e run"* — false; the gate branch falls through to
   ownership stamping and the review engine, hundreds of lines later.

   in a child, which inherits a *duplicate* of the same open file description; the parent's copy
   keeps the lock regardless.

`[[ "${_lv2_e2e_lock_kind}" == "flock" ]] && exec 9>&-` (and reset `_lv2_e2e_lock_kind=""`),
plus a regression case asserting a second acquisition succeeds immediately after release.

VERIFY_VERDICT: upheld

DELIVERABLE_COMPLETE

Target file: plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh
Diff: docs/handoff/E2E-GATE-ARCH-01/build-attempt-2.diff

## Finding under test
High/correctness: fd 9 is inherited by the suite subshell and every descendant;
any lingering background child keeps the flock's open file description alive
and wedges the global lock after the owning lane exits.

## Evidence (diff line numbers, build-attempt-2.diff)
- Line 60: `exec 9>"${_lv2_e2e_lock}" || return 2` — opens fd 9 directly in the
  calling shell (function `_lv2_e2e_acquire_lock`), not inside a subshell.
  No `9>&-` close anywhere in the diff.
- Line 61: `flock -x -w "${_wait}" 9` locks that fd.
- Lines 66-69 (`_lv2_e2e_run`): body is
  `( cd "${_lv2_e2e_root}" && bash -c "${e2e_cmd} --scope changed" )` — a
  subshell that execs `bash -c "${e2e_cmd} ..."`.
- Lines 91/104: `_lv2_e2e_run >> "${HANDOFF}/e2e-gate.log" 2>&1; e2e_rc=$?` —
  called as a plain function call from the shell that holds fd 9, so the
  subshell and the execed `bash -c` process inherit fd 9 open.

  (`rm -f .../pid; rmdir ...`). It contains no `exec 9>&-` or equivalent, so
  it does not close fd 9 for the flock path — confirms the sibling Critical
  finding and is consistent with the mechanism this High finding depends on.

## Analysis
Bash does not set close-on-exec on a numeric fd opened via `exec 9>file`
unless explicitly closed. Since fd 9 is opened in the parent shell (not
scoped into a subshell) and `_lv2_e2e_run`'s inner subshell/exec chain never
closes it, every process forked or exec'd inside that chain — the subshell,
the execed `bash -c "${e2e_cmd} --scope changed"`, and any background job
that script itself launches with `&` — inherits an open, locked duplicate of
fd 9's file description. flock's exclusive lock is tied to the open file
description, which persists as long as ANY process holds a duplicate open,
independent of the original owning process's lifetime. A background child
spawned by the e2e suite that outlives the suite run (e.g., a server process
left running) would keep that file description open and the lock held even
after the owning lane's top-level script exits and its own fd 9 is closed at
process teardown.

This is a concrete, diff-grounded mechanism, not speculative — the code as
written has no barrier (subshell fd closure, `2>&-`-style close, `exec`
inside a `(...)` with fd redirected only locally) that would prevent
inheritance.

  pre-existing ledger call at `leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh:81`, which is unrelated
